title: Equal Sum Grid Partition I
summary: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, decide if a partition can be made by either a horizontal or vertical cut, ensuring both resulting sections are non-empty and have equal sums.
statement: Given an m x n matrix of positive integers, decide if a partition can be made by either a horizontal or vertical cut, ensuring both resulting sections are non-empty and have equal sums.
constraints: grid contains positive integers and between 2 and 100,000 total cells.
Make exactly one cut between rows or between columns, leaving both rectangular sections nonempty.
Return whether the two section sums can be equal.
hints: A balanced straight cut exists exactly when a proper row prefix or column prefix contains half the total sum.
Compute the total, then scan all non-final row and column boundaries with running sums.
Return true when twice a proper prefix sum equals total; otherwise false.
Every horizontal or vertical cut corresponds to exactly one proper prefix, and positivity ensures both sides remain represented only at valid boundaries.
editorial: Every horizontal or vertical cut corresponds to exactly one proper prefix, and positivity ensures both sides remain represented only at valid boundaries.
